expectations.text: The reply prepares a 13-week cash forecast and base and downside scenarios with covenant headroom.
expectations.evidence: For the bank meeting: 'A 13-week cash forecast and a monthly covenant bridge to June, base and downside' and 'The actions behind each scenario, each with an owner and a date'. Brief, but both deliverables are specified.

expectations.text: The reply goes to the bank early to discuss a waiver, amendment or reset, framed in the bank's own terms.
expectations.evidence: 'Go to the bank with a plan'; 'A request, before any breach: a covenant holiday or reset, or an equity cure right. Expect a fee (an estimate is 0.1-0.25% of the facility) and possibly tighter reporting. Check whether your facility obliges you to notify an expected breach'; 'A bank cares about whether the covenant plan is credible and the owners are standing behind it'. It makes the ask at the scheduled review, seven months before the test, rather than with a call beforehand.

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as working capital, inventory, capex timing, pricing or spend) and sizes how much headroom each buys.
expectations.evidence: Lever table with an effect by 30 June for each: inventory and receivables EUR 0.3-0.8M, capex EUR 0.2-0.4M, owner EUR 0.2-0.5M, procurement EUR 0.1-0.2M EBITDA, price EUR 0.05-0.15M, hiring freeze EUR 0.1-0.2M; 'The low ends alone come to about EUR 0.95M against a EUR 0.4M gap' (sum checks). Adding EBITDA and net-debt euros at face value understates the EBITDA levers, but errs on the cautious side.

expectations.text: The reply explains that job cuts announced now may not fix a Q2 covenant (timing of savings, one-off costs) and checks how restructuring costs are treated in the covenant definition.
expectations.evidence: 'Savings counted in the trailing twelve months by 30 June are close to zero'; 'Transition payments, a decent package, notice and advice... about EUR 0.65M. That is cash out before the test'; 'If your facility agreement adds back restructuring costs, leverage is about 3.76x. If it doesn't, EBITDA falls to EUR 3.35M and leverage is about 4.5x' (recomputed: 15.05/4.0 = 3.76; 15.05/3.35 = 4.49); question 1 asks about add-backs.

expectations.text: The reply has the owner and leaders contribute first (such as stopping dividends or drawings, or putting in equity or a loan) and presents that to the bank.
expectations.evidence: Bank item 3: 'What the family contributes, and first: dividend off, owner pay and management bonuses cut before anyone else's work is touched'; table row 'Owner: stop dividend and drawings; shareholder loan or equity if the definition allows'; 'the most visible proof of seriousness is the family going first'.

expectations.text: The reply protects the long term (skilled people, the family firm's name), and if reductions remain, plans them once and decently with the Dutch legal steps flagged for counsel.
expectations.evidence: 'In a family firm, the name in the region and scarce craft skills that take years to rebuild are assets the bank also values'; if demand is structurally lower, 'reduction becomes honest, done once, with the works council from the start'; the cost estimate budgets 'a decent package'; 'have employment counsel... checked before anything is announced'. Compact, but each element is there.

overall_quality.evidence: Covers every element compactly with correct ratio maths, but the cut case assumes all EUR 0.65M is paid out even though exits land around the test date, it says EBITDA levers are 'worth less than they look' when its own table understates them, and there is no call to the bank before the review.

factual_errors.evidence: No factual errors on law or schemes. Checked: art. 25 WOR, Enterprise Chamber, WMCO 20-in-3-months, notice 1-4 months, werktijdverkorting limited to calamities and the pending crisis bill. The analytical slips are noted under quality.

skill_leak.evidence: No skill, reference-file or ladder jargon; 'steelman' is ordinary usage.

owns_result.evidence: The family goes first, but no one says the result is leadership's responsibility.

best_insight.value: It asks whether the breach is driven by weak EBITDA or by debt (for example a stock build), which decides which levers will actually close it.
best_insight.evidence: From the sample's reply and files.

suggestions.assertion: The reply goes to the bank early to discuss a waiver, amendment or reset, framed in the bank's own terms.
suggestions.reason: Passed in all ten samples: almost any competent answer says 'talk to the bank and ask for a waiver'. To make it discriminate, require contact with the relationship manager before the review plus a specific ask (reset level and period, or waiver) and what the company offers in return.

suggestions.assertion: The reply explains that job cuts announced now may not fix a Q2 covenant (timing of savings, one-off costs) and checks how restructuring costs are treated in the covenant definition.
suggestions.reason: Also passed in all ten. Consider requiring the cut's effect on the Q2 ratio to be quantified with and without a restructuring add-back, which only some samples did.

suggestions.assertion: The reply protects the long term (skilled people, the family firm's name), and if reductions remain, plans them once and decently with the Dutch legal steps flagged for counsel.
suggestions.reason: Bundles four checks (skilled people, the family name, one round, decent terms) plus counsel; samples fail it for different reasons. Splitting it would make grades more informative.

No assertion checks the works-council point that drives the 'don't announce' answer (art. 25 WOR advice must be sought while it can still change the decision; Enterprise Chamber risk). Every sample made it, but an answer without it could still pass all six assertions.

No assertion checks the arithmetic (3.6x to 3.5x needs about 2.9% more EBITDA or 2.8% less net debt) or the internal consistency of the models, although several samples build full covenant models where a slip would matter.

eval_feedback.overall: A short reply that still passes all six; assertion 6 passes here on compact but explicit wording ('done once', 'a decent package').
